question.text: Under Section 18A of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956, derivative contracts are legal and valid if they are:

answer.text: Traded on a recognized stock exchange and settled through the clearing house of that exchange
Executed between two parties with a written agreement, regardless of venue
Approved by SEBI on a case-by-case basis before execution
Registered with the RBI and traded through authorized dealers

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 18A of SCRA, as set out in the workbook, treats derivative contracts as legal and valid if (a) they are traded on a recognized stock exchange and (b) they are settled on the clearing house of that recognized stock exchange in accordance with its rules and bye-laws. Both conditions must be met for the contract to be legally valid. The Trap: A bilateral written agreement, individual SEBI per-contract approval, or RBI authorised-dealer routing do not, by themselves, satisfy Section 18A. Note: Lock in the two-part test: exchange-traded plus exchange clearing-house settled. Separate legal treatment of OTC derivatives lies outside this Section 18A test and is not implied by the workbook here.
